newsitem.title: CHINA: HK STOCKS SEEN MOVING LOWER, FOCUS ON H-SHARES.
newsitem.headline: HK STOCKS SEEN MOVING LOWER, FOCUS ON H-SHARES.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to move lower on Thursday on the weakness of properties and following an easier overnight close on Wall Street but H-shares and red-chips should continue to attract buyers, brokers said.
"The Hang Seng is likely to fall to 16,400 since property stocks looked weak after banks raised mortgage rates," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hang Seng Index rose 99.52 points, or 0.61 percent, to close Wednesday at 16,482.93. Later the Hang Seng London Reference Index edged 6.70 points higher to 16,489.63.
The Dow industrials lost 32.52 points to close at 7,928.32.
The market was still in a consolidation mode but sentiment remained positive with plenty of liquidity around, said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"I think the Hang Seng should trade within a 100 point range today," he said.
"Investors have shifted their focus from blue chips to red chips and H-shares," Mak added.
H-shares continued to surge on Wednesday with the Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index soaring 94.75 points, or 6.61 percent to close at 1,528.70.
